knowledge_point.title: Simplifying Expressions in Degrees Using the Sum and Difference Formulas

question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the difference formula for sine:
$$
\sin(u-v)=\sin u\cos v-\cos u\sin v.
$$
Use the sum formula for sine:
$$
\sin(u+v)=\sin u\cos v+\cos u\sin v.
$$
Expand the two terms separately:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\sin(x-30^\circ)&=\sin x\cos 30^\circ-\cos x\sin 30^\circ\\
&=\sin x\cdot\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)-\cos x\cdot\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\\
&=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\sin x-\frac{1}{2}\cos x
\end{aligned}
$$
$$
\begin{aligned}
\sin(x+30^\circ)&=\sin x\cos 30^\circ+\cos x\sin 30^\circ\\
&=\sin x\cdot\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)+\cos x\cdot\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\\
&=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\sin x+\frac{1}{2}\cos x
\end{aligned}
$$
Let $E$ denote the original expression. Subtract the entire second expansion and collect like terms:
$$
\begin{aligned}
E&=\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\right)\sin x\\
&\quad+\left(-\frac{1}{2}-\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\right)\cos x\\
&=\left(0\right)\sin x\\
&\quad+\left(-1\right)\cos x
\end{aligned}
$$
Thus $A=0$ and $B=-1$.

knowledge_point.title: Simplifying Expressions in Degrees Using the Sum and Difference Formulas

question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the sum formula for sine:
$$
\sin(u+v)=\sin u\cos v+\cos u\sin v.
$$
Use the sum formula for sine:
$$
\sin(u+v)=\sin u\cos v+\cos u\sin v.
$$
Expand the two terms separately:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\sin(x+120^\circ)&=\sin x\cos 120^\circ+\cos x\sin 120^\circ\\
&=\sin x\cdot\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)+\cos x\cdot\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\\
&=-\frac{1}{2}\sin x+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cos x
\end{aligned}
$$
$$
\begin{aligned}
\sin(x+210^\circ)&=\sin x\cos 210^\circ+\cos x\sin 210^\circ\\
&=\sin x\cdot\left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)+\cos x\cdot\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)\\
&=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\sin x-\frac{1}{2}\cos x
\end{aligned}
$$
Let $E$ denote the original expression. Add the entire second expansion and collect like terms:
$$
\begin{aligned}
E&=\left(-\frac{1}{2}+\left(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\right)\sin x\\
&\quad+\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)\right)\cos x\\
&=\left(-\frac{1+\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\sin x\\
&\quad+\left(\frac{-1+\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\cos x
\end{aligned}
$$
Thus $A=-\frac{1+\sqrt{3}}{2}$ and $B=\frac{-1+\sqrt{3}}{2}$.
